name: sidebar-layout
title: Sidebar layout
description: A sidebar beside content that wraps above it by itself when the content gets too narrow, with no breakpoints.
docs: sidebar and children are the two columns; side is start or end, and the DOM follows what people see on the wide layout, so a start sidebar comes first and an end sidebar last. sidebarWidth is the width the sidebar prefers (18rem) and contentMin the least share of the row the content may have (60%): when the content would fall below it, the sidebar wraps onto its own line and fills it. The switch reads the space the layout has, not the viewport, so it works in a dialog, a sheet or a narrow card; it happens at (sidebarWidth + gap) / (1 - contentMin). gap is none, sm, md or lg, or any length. sticky pins the sidebar while the content scrolls (true for 1rem from the top, or a length such as 5rem to clear a header); it only pins while the two are side by side, and the sidebar scrolls inside itself when it is taller than the screen. Pinning makes the layout a size container, so it has to fill its parent.
